# Telegram

4 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 3 standard (1 credit), 1 custom (flat/metered) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

## GET /v1/telegram/post - 1 credit (standard)

Returns one public Telegram post by its t.me URL, including the text, publish time, view count, the per-emoji reaction breakdown, and direct media URLs. View and reaction counts on posts are rounded by Telegram's own public preview, so use them for ranking rather than for exact deltas.

**Use when** you have a single post link and do not want to page the whole channel. View and reaction counts are rounded, so read them as ranking signals rather than exact figures.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Public Telegram post URL, in the form https://t.me/{handle}/{id} · e.g. `https://t.me/durov/546`

**Response** `Post` object at `data`, `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/Post.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+12 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {display_name}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {likes, views}; `post.ext` {reaction_counts}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.author` {avatar_url null, verified null}; `post.engagement` {comments null, shares null, saves null}; `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null} (+3 more).

**Next** `telegram/profile/posts` (`handle` ← `data.post.author.username`) - List Telegram channel posts. · `telegram/profile` (`handle` ← `data.post.author.username`) - Get Telegram channel profile.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/telegram/post" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://t.me/durov/546" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/telegram/profile - 1 credit (standard)

Returns a public Telegram channel or group profile including its display name, description, avatar URL, verification status, and subscriber count. The subscriber count is exact rather than abbreviated. Private channels, invite-only groups, and channels with no public preview return 404.

**Use when** you have a handle and want the channel snapshot, or to confirm a channel is public before paging its posts.
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - Public Telegram handle, with or without the leading @, or a t.me channel URL · e.g. `telegram`

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |

+9 more (types in the full schema): `author` {followers, verified}; `computed` {content_category, engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `author.ext` {business_hours, products}. Also in the sample: `author` {following null, posts_count null, likes_count null}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/telegram/profile" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=telegram" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/telegram/profile/posts - 1 credit (standard)

Returns one page of recent public posts from a Telegram channel or group, newest page first. Each post carries its text, publish time, view count, the per-emoji reaction breakdown, and direct media URLs for photos and videos. Pass the returned cursor to walk further back through the channel's history. Page size varies because photo albums count as one post and service messages are skipped, so a short page does not mean the end of the channel: keep paging until the cursor is absent. Send `q` to search inside the channel instead: you get one page of the newest messages that contain every word of `q` (up to about 20), at the same price, with no cursor.

**Use when** you want to read or archive a channel's history. Page size varies, so keep passing the cursor until it comes back empty rather than stopping on a short page.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** cursor · ≈20/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/20) x 1 credits · typical 2.9-7.3 s

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - Public Telegram handle, with or without the leading @, or a t.me channel URL · e.g. `telegram`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Cursor from the previous page's pagination block. Omit it for the most recent posts.
- `q` (optional, string) - Words to search for inside the channel, for example `cheap watches`. Returns one page of the newest messages whose text contains every word (put a phrase in double quotes to require it as written), at the same price as a plain page. Telegram's own search also matches other forms of a word (`watch` for `watches`); those messages are left out, because they do not contain the words. A search page has no cursor, so `q` cannot be combined with `cursor`.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Response** `PostList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/PostList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.published_at` | Post creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string. |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |

+12 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {engagement_rate, estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.author` {display_name}; `post.content` {duration_seconds, media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.engagement` {likes, views}; `post.ext` {reaction_counts}; `post.flags` {deleted}. Also in the sample: `post.author` {avatar_url null, verified null}; `post.engagement` {comments null, shares null, saves null}; `post.flags` {nsfw null, spoiler null} (+1 more). Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

**Next** `telegram/post` (`url` ← `data.items[].post.url`) - Get Telegram post.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/telegram/profile/posts" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=telegram" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/telegram/search - 2-16 credits (request-shaped)

Finds public Telegram channels by keyword, so you can pick the channels to read with `/v1/telegram/profile` and `/v1/telegram/profile/posts`. Channels are discovered through a public web search index limited to t.me pages, so this finds what that index has already seen: it is not real time, a channel or message from the last few days may not appear yet, and private channels and invite-only groups never appear. Returns one row per channel, in the order the search found them, on the same Author shape `/v1/telegram/profile` returns: `author.username` is the public handle (pass it as `handle`), `author.url` is `https://t.me/<handle>`, and `author.display_name` is the channel's title when the search result carried it (null when the result showed only the handle). `author.ext.search_hit` says how the channel was found: `match` is `channel_page` (the channel's own page) or `post_in_channel` (a message or the message preview), `title` and `snippet` are the hit as the index showed it, `evidence_url` is the first page that matched, and `matched_urls` lists every t.me page the search matched for that channel, so you can open the exact messages. The snippet is the index's text, not the channel's description, so `author.bio` stays null on a plain call, as do `author.followers`, `author.avatar_url` and `author.verified`. Send `include=details` and every channel is joined, in the same call, to the profile lookup: the exact subscriber count (`author.followers`), the description (`author.bio`), the avatar, the verified flag and, where it was null, the title land on each row. Words in `query` match loosely; put a phrase in double quotes to require it, and add `-word` to exclude a word. Cost: 2 credits for the page, plus 1 credit per channel filled from a fresh lookup with `include=details` (at most 10 a page, so 12 credits at most); channels already in cache are free, channels that could not be filled are refunded, and a search that finds no public channel is a 404 at 0 credits. Time: a plain page takes about 2 to 12 seconds; `include=details` adds a few seconds on a fresh page (the lookups run in parallel and the call waits for the slowest, never more than 10 seconds) and nothing when the channels are already cached. The response carries a `hydration` block itemising rows, lookups, cache hits, credits and milliseconds. A page holds up to 10 channels, fewer when several hits belong to one channel. Forward `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor` for the next page; the same channel can appear again on a later page. Keyword hits include coupon and reseller channels that merely contain your words: send `relevance=filter` to drop the channels that are not about your query, or add `relevant_to=` with a sentence describing the channels you want (for example `shops selling cheap or replica watches`) to judge them against that instead; each channel is judged on its title and the search snippet.

**Use when** you want to find channels selling or discussing a product or brand, then read them with profile/posts. The index lags behind Telegram, so treat it as discovery, not a live feed.
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 2 credits for the page. include=details holds 1 credit per channel (at most 10 a page, fewer with limit) and keeps only the channels filled from a fresh lookup, so a page is at most 12 credits; channels served from cache are free, unfilled channels are refunded, and a search that finds no public channel costs 0. Relevance against your query (by default, or with relevance=) is free. Adding relevant_to= holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 rows that were newly judged: rows already judged for the same topic are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free. With `max_pages`, `max_items` or `max_credits`, each page walked is billed at this price (a cached page is free), and `max_credits` caps the total.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · default page size not measured; set with `limit` · depth unknown · typical 2.3-9.6 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Keywords describing the channels or messages to find, for example `byd spare parts`. Put a phrase in double quotes to require it. Keywords only: the search is already limited to public Telegram pages, so a `site:` operator is refused before billing. · e.g. `byd spare parts`
- `page` (optional, integer, min 1) - Page number, starting at 1. Forwarding `pagination.next_cursor` as `cursor` does the same.
- `date_posted` (optional, enum: last-hour | last-day | last-week | last-month | last-year) - Only pages the search index dates within this window: last-hour, last-day, last-week, last-month or last-year. Useful for monitoring new activity.
- `region` (optional, string) - Two-letter country code (US, AE, IN, KR) whose results to prefer.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-10) - Return at most this many channels from the page (1 to 10). With `include=details` it also lowers the credits held, one per channel.
- `include` (optional, enum: details) - Set to `details` (one token only) to fill, on every channel in this one call, `author.followers` (the exact subscriber count), `author.bio` (the description), `author.avatar_url`, `author.verified`, and the title where it was null. Holds 1 credit per channel (at most 10 a page) and keeps only the channels filled from a fresh lookup; channels already in cache and channels the lookup cannot fill are refunded, so a page is never more than 12 credits. Read `data.hydration` for the rows, the credits held and kept, and the time. Without it the call is unchanged.
- **Shared controls** `relevance` (score | filter) · `relevant_to` · `relevance_threshold` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality); `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Constraints**

- `relevance_threshold`, `relevant_to` are no-ops without `relevance` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.ext.search_hit.title` | The hit title as the search index showed it. |
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.username` | User handle or username |
| `author.avatar_url` | URL to profile picture (with `include=details`) |
| `author.bio` | Profile biography or description (with `include=details`) |

+10 more (types in the full schema): `author` {display_name, followers, verified}; `computed` {relevance}; `author.ext` {business_hours, products}; `author.ext.search_hit` {evidence_url, match, matched_urls, snippet}. Never filled: `author.following`, `author.joined_at`, `author.likes_count`, `author.posts_count`, `author.private`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.hydration`, `data.relevance`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/telegram/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=byd spare parts" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
